title: Design a Distributed Agentic CLI Coding Platform (Claude Code)

spark.summary: Design an end-to-end agentic CLI coding platform supporting millions of developers, local OS sandboxing, 85%+ prompt-cache hit rates, parallel MCP subagents, and enterprise auditability.
spark.keyTakeaway: If model quality drifts from offline training baselines, keep execution local inside Seatbelt/seccomp + shadow Git worktrees while routing inference through an ephemeral prefix-cache-aware cloud gateway.
spark.byteSummary:
Designing a distributed agentic CLI platform like Claude Code spans both a local client runtime (Rust/Go binary) and a cloud inference control plane. Locally, the CLI must execute arbitrary builds, linters, and git operations with zero network round-trip overhead for file reads, while protecting the host OS from destructive commands or prompt injection via Seatbelt/seccomp sandboxes and a declarative permission policy engine.

In the cloud, the platform handles bursty multi-turn tool loops where each session sends 20-100 sequential requests with growing context. To prevent prohibitive GPU costs and multi-second TTFT, the cloud gateway routes each session to sticky KV-prefix replicas, supports 90%-fill auto-compaction, and coordinates parallel read-only subagent calls.

Enterprise deployments add centralized policy enforcement (managed allow/deny lists), zero-data-retention (ZDR) inference routing, and asynchronous OpenTelemetry cost/tool-use auditing without slowing down the developer's interactive terminal.

learningJourney.title: Split Local-Cloud Control Plane & Latency Budget
learningJourney.purpose: Decide which components run on the developer's machine versus the cloud inference cluster.

explanation.foundation: File reads, ripgrep, AST parsing, and test execution MUST run locally to avoid uploading gigabytes of proprietary source code and adding network latency per tool call.
explanation.core: Only compacted prompts, tool schemas, and tool outputs cross TLS to the cloud LLM gateway.
explanation.deepDive: Target <400ms TTFT on cached turns and <50ms local tool dispatch.

learningJourney.title: Shadow Git Worktrees & Parallel Safe Execution
learningJourney.purpose: Isolate agent edits from dirty working trees and enable atomic multi-file rollback.

explanation.foundation: Developers often invoke the CLI in a repo with uncommitted changes.
explanation.core: Before the agent mutates any file, the CLI captures a baseline shadow Git tree (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=.git/agent-shadow-index git write-tree`).
explanation.deepDive: For speculative multi-approach fixes or background test runs, the CLI can spin up an isolated `git worktree` so the user's primary editor buffer is never disrupted.

cards.label: Instant Rollback
cards.detail: Restoring a shadow tree SHA reverts 50+ file edits in milliseconds.

sectionDiagram.summary: Shadow Git indices and worktrees protect uncommitted developer work during autonomous runs.
sectionDiagram.caption: Worktree isolation allows tests to run without locking the user's active IDE.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design a Distributed Agentic CLI Coding Platform (Claude Code) without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: If model quality drifts from offline training baselines, keep execution local inside Seatbelt/seccomp + shadow Git worktrees while routing inference through an ephemeral prefix-cache-aware cloud gateway.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

learningJourney.title: Enterprise Permission Policy & Kernel Sandboxing
learningJourney.purpose: Enforce organization-wide security rules and kernel-level filesystem/network jails.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Enterprise Permission Policy & Kernel Sandboxing** as the intuition layer for Design a Distributed Agentic CLI Coding Platform (Claude Code): Enforce organization-wide security rules and kernel-level filesystem/network jails.
explanation.core: Enterprises push signed policy JSON (`managed-settings.json`) specifying forbidden paths (`**/.env`, `**/secrets/**`), blocked binaries (`rm -rf`, `curl`), and allowed MCP servers. The CLI evaluates policies deterministically before spawning any subprocess inside macOS Seatbelt or Linux seccomp/landlock, ensuring even a compromised MCP tool output cannot exfiltrate credentials.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, enterprise permission policy & kernel sandboxing becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Scale to enterprise monorepos with concurrent read-only MCP subagents, Bash AST inspection, and headless CI/CD runners.

learningJourney.title: Ephemeral Prefix-Cache Routing in the Cloud Gateway
learningJourney.purpose: Route 100-turn CLI sessions to warm KV-cache GPUs for 85%+ cache hits.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Ephemeral Prefix-Cache Routing in the Cloud Gateway** as the intuition layer for Design a Distributed Agentic CLI Coding Platform (Claude Code): Route 100-turn CLI sessions to warm KV-cache GPUs for 85%+ cache hits.
explanation.core: CLI coding sessions have a 5-minute TTL between turns as developers review diffs. The Cloud Gateway hashes the first 4KB of the system+tools+repo-map prefix plus `session_id` to route requests via consistent hashing to GPU clusters holding those KV blocks in HBM or fast NVMe L2 cache, cutting per-turn prefill cost by up to 90%.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, ephemeral prefix-cache routing in the cloud gateway becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Scale to enterprise monorepos with concurrent read-only MCP subagents, Bash AST inspection, and headless CI/CD runners.

learningJourney.title: 90% Context Budget Manager & Auto-Compaction
learningJourney.purpose: Keep multi-hour debugging sessions within token limits without losing active bug context.

explanation.foundation: Think of **90% Context Budget Manager & Auto-Compaction** as the intuition layer for Design a Distributed Agentic CLI Coding Platform (Claude Code): Keep multi-hour debugging sessions within token limits without losing active bug context.
explanation.core: The CLI tracks exact token counts from API usage headers (`input_tokens + cache_read_tokens`). At 90% of the model's window, the Context Budget Manager runs a two-phase compaction: first replacing older `tool_result` blobs (>1,000 tokens) with `[pruned: path/lines]`, then invoking a structured compaction prompt to distill older turns into a dense engineering handoff summary.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, 90% context budget manager & auto-compaction becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Scale to enterprise monorepos with concurrent read-only MCP subagents, Bash AST inspection, and headless CI/CD runners.

cards.label: Deterministic Trigger
cards.detail: Compact proactively at 90% so the next tool output never hits a hard 400 error.

sectionDiagram.summary: Proactive two-phase compaction prevents mid-task context overflow.
sectionDiagram.caption: Pruning bulky tool logs before summarizing preserves key architectural decisions.

learningJourney.title: Parallel MCP Subagent Spawner & Shared Repo Cache
learningJourney.purpose: Accelerate large-monorepo investigations with concurrent read-only subagents.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Parallel MCP Subagent Spawner & Shared Repo Cache** as the intuition layer for Design a Distributed Agentic CLI Coding Platform (Claude Code): Accelerate large-monorepo investigations with concurrent read-only subagents.
explanation.core: When asked to trace an end-to-end bug across frontend, API, and database layers, the CLI spawns 3 concurrent read-only subagents. Each subagent shares the local read-only AST/ripgrep index and connects to scoped MCP servers (e.g., Sentry, Datadog, GitHub), returning structured summaries that the main agent synthesizes into a single coordinated patch.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, parallel mcp subagent spawner & shared repo cache becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Scale to enterprise monorepos with concurrent read-only MCP subagents, Bash AST inspection, and headless CI/CD runners.

learningJourney.title: Headless CI/CD Mode, Webhook Triggers & Fleet Telemetry
learningJourney.purpose: Run the same agentic harness unattended in GitHub Actions for PR review and test fixing.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Headless CI/CD Mode, Webhook Triggers & Fleet Telemetry** as the intuition layer for Design a Distributed Agentic CLI Coding Platform (Claude Code): Run the same agentic harness unattended in GitHub Actions for PR review and test fixing.
explanation.core: With `--headless --output-format json`, the CLI runs non-interactively in CI runners: no TUI, strict read/test allowlists, and a hard dollar/turn budget cap (`--max-turns 15 --max-budget-usd 1.50`). Structured JSON outcomes (patch diff, test pass status, token cost) post directly back to the PR via GitHub Apps.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, headless ci/cd mode, webhook triggers & fleet telemetry becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. knowledgeChecks.question: Why must file reading, ripgrep search, and test execution run locally on the developer's machine rather than in the cloud?

options.text: Cloud servers cannot run ripgrep or git.
options.feedback: Cloud containers can run ripgrep, but syncing the entire local repo on every edit is prohibitive.

options.text: It avoids uploading entire proprietary repos, eliminates network latency per local tool call, and works with uncommitted local state.
options.feedback: Correct! Local execution keeps gigabytes of source code private and gives sub-50ms tool latency.

options.text: Because LLM APIs do not support JSON over HTTPS.
options.feedback: LLM APIs use JSON/SSE over HTTPS; local execution is for repo privacy and latency.
Cloud gateways still use prompt-prefix caching for the conversation.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Running tools locally keeps proprietary code on-device except for targeted slices, operates on uncommitted edits, and avoids network round trips for every grep or test.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does the platform preserve KV-prefix cache hits when a developer takes 4 minutes to review a proposed diff before approving the next turn?

options.text: Offload evicted HBM KV-cache blocks to fast local NVMe L2 storage with a 30-minute TTL.
options.feedback: Correct! NVMe L2 KV offloading bridges multi-minute human think times without exhausting scarce GPU HBM.

options.text: Lock the GPU exclusively for that user for 30 minutes.
options.feedback: Idle GPU reservation would waste 95% of cluster compute.

options.text: Send dummy keepalive tokens to the LLM every 100ms.
options.feedback: Dummy inference calls would waste compute and corrupt context.

options.text: Disable Seatbelt sandboxing on the client.
options.feedback: Client sandboxing is unrelated to cloud KV-cache retention.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: GPU HBM is too scarce to pin idle sessions for minutes, but NVMe L2 offloading retains KV prefixes cheaply and promotes them back in milliseconds on the next turn.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which guardrails are essential when running an agentic CLI coding harness in headless CI/CD mode?

options.text: Interactive TUI color diffs and infinite retry loops.
options.feedback: Headless CI has no interactive TTY, and infinite retries burn budget.

options.text: A strict allowlist of non-destructive tools, ephemeral container isolation, and hard max-turn and max-USD budget caps.
options.feedback: Correct! Unattended CI runs require strict tool allowlists and hard turn/spend caps to prevent runaway costs.

options.text: Disabling all unit tests so the agent finishes faster.
options.feedback: Tests are the primary verification signal for coding agents.

options.text: Granting root host filesystem access to the container.
options.feedback: CI runners should always use least-privilege ephemeral isolation.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Headless CI agents operate without human-in-the-loop prompts, making ephemeral isolation, tool allowlists, and hard turn/USD caps mandatory.

beginner.summary: Design a CLI coding agent platform that runs tools safely on a developer's laptop while using cloud GPUs for reasoning.
beginner.keyTakeaway: If model quality drifts from offline training baselines, keep execution local inside Seatbelt/seccomp + shadow Git worktrees while routing inference through an ephemeral prefix-cache-aware cloud gateway.
beginner.byteSummary:
A distributed CLI coding platform splits work between the user's laptop and the cloud. The local app searches files, shows diffs, and runs tests inside a security sandbox so bad commands can't harm the system.

The cloud side hosts the LLM and caches the conversation prefix so follow-up turns stay fast and affordable.

intermediate.summary: Architect local-cloud split control planes, shadow Git worktrees, kernel sandboxes, and 90% auto-compaction.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: If model quality drifts from offline training baselines, keep execution local inside Seatbelt/seccomp + shadow Git worktrees while routing inference through an ephemeral prefix-cache-aware cloud gateway.
intermediate.byteSummary:
The local Rust/Go binary manages TUI streaming, shadow Git snapshots for instant rollback, and signed enterprise policies enforced via Seatbelt/Landlock. Only compacted prompts cross TLS to the cloud gateway.

In the cloud, consistent hashing routes turns to GPU clusters with HBM + NVMe L2 KV-prefix caches, surviving multi-minute developer review pauses while keeping TTFT under 400ms.

advanced.summary: Scale to enterprise monorepos with concurrent read-only MCP subagents, Bash AST inspection, and headless CI/CD runners.
advanced.keyTakeaway: If model quality drifts from offline training baselines, keep execution local inside Seatbelt/seccomp + shadow Git worktrees while routing inference through an ephemeral prefix-cache-aware cloud gateway.
advanced.byteSummary:
Enterprise deployments add Bash AST parsing to block obfuscated command chaining, ZDR encrypted ephemeral KV caches, and bounded-concurrency read-only MCP subagents for cross-service debugging.

The same harness runs in headless CI/CD containers via `--headless --output-format json` with strict tool allowlists and hard USD/turn circuit breakers.
